title: World cinema
tagline: From Amélie to Andrei Rublev without noticing the water got hot.

levels.name: Popcorn
levels.note: A Paris waitress, a fake GDR, revenge, ramen, a nose and spiked gazpacho.

levels.name: Easy charmers
levels.note: A projectionist, a spring, cricket, a butcher, Hulot and a sung musical.

levels.name: Modern masters
levels.note: Basements, banlieue, Wong Kar-wai, Kieślowski and Zhang Yimou.

levels.name: The deep end
levels.note: Herzog up the Amazon, chess with Death and the Apu trilogy.

levels.name: Cooked
levels.note: Only if they finish Andrei Rublev and ask for more.

core.b: Jean-Pierre Jeunet's shy Parisian waitress secretly fixes strangers' lives. Pure sugar, gorgeously shot. The easiest subtitles you'll ever read.

br.note: Jeunet's junkyard gang takes on arms dealers
Michel Gondry's cardboard dream world

core.b: A son hides the fall of the Berlin Wall from his bedridden socialist mother, faking East German TV news. Funny and sweet.

br.note: A Stasi agent bugs a playwright's flat and starts to care
A prankster dad embarrasses his corporate daughter. Long, very funny

core.b: Six Argentine stories of people snapping: a plane, a road-rage duel, a wedding from hell. Savage and hilarious.

br.note: Argentine thriller, Oscar winner, the stadium shot
Danish teachers test a theory about staying slightly drunk

core.b: Juzo Itami's 'ramen western': a trucker in a cowboy hat helps a widow perfect her noodle shop, with sketches about food and sex in between.

br.note: Itami's comedy about a dogged tax inspector
Two Italian brothers, one feast

core.b: Depardieu with the nose, the sword and the verse, writing love letters for a prettier man. Swashbuckling and heartbreaking.

br.note: Steve Martin's modern Cyrano
Depardieu as a man who may not be who he says

core.t: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
core.b: Almodóvar's screwball farce: a dumped actress, spiked gazpacho, terrorists and a burning bed. Antonio Banderas.

br.note: Almodóvar's love letter to women and actresses
Penélope Cruz, a body in a freezer and a ghost
Two men at the bedsides of comatose women
Banderas as an ageing Almodóvar

core.b: A Sicilian boy and the village projectionist. Sentimental, yes, but the kissing montage gets everyone.

br.note: Pablo Neruda teaches a postman poetry
Benigni's Holocaust comedy. Loved and loathed

core.b: Provence, a hunchback city man (Depardieu) and two peasants (Montand, Auteuil) who block his spring. Gripping slow tragedy.

seq.note: The revenge. Watch them back to back

core.b: Villagers in 1893 India bet their tax on a cricket match against the British. Nearly four hours of songs and sport, and it flies.

br.note: The Bollywood romance that ran 25 years in one cinema
Bollywood college comedy
Five-hour Indian gangster saga

core.b: Jeunet and Caro: a post-apocalyptic butcher feeds his tenants to his tenants. The squeaky-bedsprings rhythm scene. Also on Sci-fi.

br.note: A mad scientist steals children's dreams

core.b: Jacques Tati's gangly, almost silent holidaymaker wrecks a seaside hotel. Gentle and perfectly timed.

br.note: Hulot versus a gadget-filled modern house
Tati's glass-and-steel Paris, built at ruinous cost

core.b: Jacques Demy's musical where every line is sung, in candy colours. A young couple, a war, an ending that wrecks you.

br.note: Demy's sunnier one, with Gene Kelly

core.b: Bong Joon-ho: a poor family worms its way into a rich family's house, and then the basement. Best Picture winner.

br.note: Bong's serial-killer procedural
Lee Chang-dong's slow-burn mystery

core.b: Mathieu Kassovitz: 24 hours with three friends from the Paris banlieue after a riot. Black and white, furious. Core on Gangster.

br.note: Ladj Ly's banlieue police drama
Jacques Audiard's prison gangster epic

core.b: Wong Kar-wai: two lovesick Hong Kong cops, a blonde-wigged smuggler and 'California Dreamin'' on repeat.

br.note: The night-time companion piece
Two men falling apart in Buenos Aires

core.b: Tony Leung and Maggie Cheung, neighbours whose spouses are cheating, almost falling in love in noodle-stall corridors. Gorgeous.
Kieślowski's trilogy starts with Juliette Binoche, widowed, trying to cut herself off from everything.

seq.note: The best, and the ending ties all three together

br.note: Two identical women in Poland and France

core.b: Zhang Yimou: Gong Li becomes the fourth wife of a lord in 1920s China, in a courtyard of rituals and rivalries.

br.note: Two Peking opera stars across fifty years of Chinese history
Edward Yang's Taipei family epic

core.b: Kurosawa: a murder in the woods told four ways by four witnesses, none agreeing. The film that taught the world unreliable narrators. Homer: 'You liked Rashomon.' Marge: 'That's not how I remember it.'

br.note: Nolan shows Troy sacked three times, differently each time
Ridley Scott tells a rape case from three sides
Zhang Yimou's colour-coded wuxia lies
The same assassination eight times. Silly
Kurosawa: a dying bureaucrat builds a playground

core.b: Kurosawa's Macbeth in feudal Japan: Toshiro Mifune, forest spirits and the arrow finale with real arrows.

br.note: Kurosawa's King Lear, in colour, enormous

core.b: Godard's jump-cut debut: Belmondo as a cocky car thief, Jean Seberg selling the Herald Tribune. The French New Wave starts here.

br.note: Truffaut's runaway boy and that final freeze frame
Truffaut's love triangle
Agnès Varda's two hours in real time

core.b: Fellini's memories of a seaside town: fascists, a tobacconist, a mad uncle up a tree and the night everyone rows out to see the liner Rex.

br.note: Fellini's liner full of opera singers and a rhinoceros
Mastroianni and the Trevi Fountain. Tedious, but famous
Giulietta Masina's hopeful prostitute

core.b: Fellini's blocked film director (Mastroianni) escapes into fantasies and memories. The ultimate film about making films.

br.note: Fellini's strongman and his simple assistant

core.b: Wim Wenders: angels drift over divided Berlin, listening to thoughts, and one falls for a trapeze artist. Peter Falk plays himself.

br.note: Wenders in America: Harry Dean Stanton walks out of the desert
Twenty minutes, three times, techno. Also on Action

core.b: Herzog sends Klaus Kinski's conquistador down the Amazon on a raft, mad with power, surrounded by monkeys.

br.note: Herzog and Kinski's vampire. Also on Horror

core.b: Herzog and Kinski again: a man who wants an opera house in the jungle drags a real steamship over a mountain.

br.note: The documentary of the chaos behind it
Herzog on Kinski, his best enemy

core.b: Bergman: a knight back from the Crusades plays chess with Death while plague crosses Sweden.

br.note: Bergman's actress and nurse blur into one. The deep end
Bergman's warm, ghostly family epic

core.b: Satyajit Ray's debut: a poor Bengali family, a boy and his sister, and a train across the fields. Inspired by Bicycle Thieves.

br.note: De Sica's father and son hunt a stolen bike in post-war Rome

core.b: Bergman: an old professor drives to collect an honour and relives his regrets on the way. Depressing, and beautiful.

br.note: Ozu's elderly couple visit children too busy for them

core.b: Tarkovsky's three-hour medieval Russia: an icon painter, a Tatar raid and a boy who casts a giant bell. The bell sequence is one of cinema's greatest.

br.note: Tarkovsky's dream of childhood
Tarkovsky's Zone. Beyond the final boss on Sci-fi
A Soviet wartime love story, astonishing camera

core.w: Long, brutal raid; real animal cruelty.

beyond.t: Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
beyond.note: Chantal Akerman: three and a half hours of a widow's chores. Sight & Sound's greatest film ever. Fuck that movie, and fuck critics.
